items.excerpt: def apply_mask(self, weights: Array, mask: Array) -> Array | BCOO
items.why_relevant: Core sparse application. Returns either dense (weights * mask) or BCOO with fixed nse=nse_budget. Line 31-32 comment: 'Eager Python-side only — NOT safe under filter_jit/jax.jit. n_true branches on a traced Array under jit → TracerBoolConversionError.' Must be called outside jit.

items.excerpt: def make_mask(self, weights: Array, step: int) -> Array
items.why_relevant: Mask generation. Uses argsort to select EXACTLY nse_budget True values (no threshold ties). Returns jnp.bool_ array with shape=weights.shape.

items.excerpt: class SparseMaskManager: (NOT an eqx.Module)
items.why_relevant: Python-side mutable mask tracker. line 28-51: step() method updates masks (if schedule says so) and applies them via tree_map_with_path. Line 33: should_update = not initialized OR policy.should_update(step). Line 51: applies via tree_map_with_path (Python-side tree traversal).

items.why_relevant: Applies current masks to params via tree_map_with_path. Returns params with sparse structure applied (BCOO or dense). Must be called OUTSIDE jit/filter_jit because apply_mask branches on traced values.

BCOO is the sparse format returned by apply_mask when nse < nse_budget. Fixed-nse padding (line 45: size=nse_budget, fill_value=0) ensures deterministic indices; validity_mask (line 46) zeros unused slots.

items.excerpt: Verifies that apply_mask returns BCOO with nse == nse_budget (fixed)
items.why_relevant: Tests confirm BCOO has fixed nse=nse_budget (line 39: assert result.nse == 4). This is the key to avoiding retrace: shape of indices and data arrays are static.

items.excerpt: Tests that padding slots (0,0) are zeroed via validity_mask
items.why_relevant: Confirms that fixed-nse BCOO correctly handles fewer True values than nse_budget: padded slots are zeroed, not aliased to weight[0,0].

items.excerpt: inference_model = eqx.nn.inference_mode(state.model)
items.why_relevant: Existing pattern: Engine.eval wraps model in eqx.nn.inference_mode before iteration (line 169). This disables dropout/stochastic layers. No sparse-aware variant yet.

items.excerpt: n_true branches on a traced Array under jit → TracerBoolConversionError
items.why_relevant: CRITICAL: apply_mask uses n_true = jnp.sum(mask) to decide fallback path (line 34-42). This is NOT safe under jit because n_true is a traced scalar. Branching on it causes retrace. Fixed-nse BCOO avoids retrace by using static size=nse_budget in argwhere (line 45).

items.excerpt: nse_budget: int
items.why_relevant: Static, non-traced constant. Used as size parameter in argwhere (fixed-size indices). Key to avoiding retrace: when apply_mask always produces BCOO with nse=nse_budget, JAX doesn't need to retrace when inputs have static shapes.

items.excerpt: @eqx.filter_jit def step(self, state: ResumableState, batch: Any) -> tuple[ResumableState, dict]
items.why_relevant: Training step is filter_jit'd. Calls loss_fn(model(batch['inputs']), ...) inside jit. If SparseMaskManager.step were called inside jit, it would fail (apply_mask not jit-safe). Must be applied before filter_jit.

items.excerpt: @eqx.filter_jit def _step_jit(self, state: ResumableState, batch: Any)
items.why_relevant: Safety variant also filter_jit'd. Same constraint: sparse mask application must occur outside jit.

items.excerpt: yield from []  # This is a placeholder implementation.
items.why_relevant: BucketIterator not yet implemented. Would be needed for padding inputs to static bucket sizes to avoid retrace when sparse weight shapes change across buckets.

patterns: apply_mask is NOT jit-safe; branching on traced n_true causes retrace. Fixed-nse BCOO via argwhere(size=nse_budget) solves this.
SparseMaskManager.step must run outside jit. Current training loop has no hook for this yet.
Inference already has eqx.nn.inference_mode pattern; can extend with sparse-aware variant.
BucketIterator is a stub; static bucket-padding strategy depends on completing this.
BCOO with fixed nse avoids retrace only if shapes don't change per-batch. Bucket-padding + static batch sizes would guarantee this.
gaps: No inference-only sparse wrapper (e.g., SparseModel or InferenceModel) yet.
No training loop hook for SparseMaskManager.step() — when/where should it be called relative to trainer.step?
BucketIterator is incomplete; can't test static-shape bucketing without it.
No documentation on how BCOO behaves in jitted matmul (sparse ops library compatibility).
No integration test showing sparse weight + forward pass without retrace.
notes: Index of 862 nodes, 3316 edges. Core sparse infrastructure (Policy, Manager, Config) is complete and tested. Inference entry point (Engine.eval) exists but doesn't use sparsity. Training loop (Engine.fit → Trainer.step) is jitted but no sparse hook yet. BucketIterator stub blocks static-shape tiling strategy. BCOO format is correct but untested in jitted code paths.

patterns: Tiling layer is split: CORE exports (AxisSpec, BatchPlanner, strategy types, iterators) always available; OPTIONAL (DedupGather, DedupSpec) imported from submodules.
BatchPlanner.plan() executes 5-phase logic: Phase 0 CarrySpec pre-demotion → Scan, Phase 0b DedupSpec pre-demotion → DedupGather, Phases 1+ standard cardinality/memory rules → Vmap/SafeMap/Bucket.
AxisStrategy is a sealed union (Vmap | SafeMap | Scan | DedupGather | Bucket) with immutable dataclass variants; each carries distinct metadata (batch_size, transition, indices, boundaries).
Iterator types are eqx.Module instances (pytree-safe); two protocols (MapIterator, ScanIterator) with 3 concrete impls (VmapIterator, SafeMapIterator, JaxScanIterator).
Bucket is a host-side plan descriptor (no device execution); select_bucket() and bucketize() both run on host before JIT; mask returned for post-hoc unmask.
No existing visualization, metrics, or display utilities in xtrax; opportunity to design EDA surface for plan objects, decision rationales, and dedup statistics.
BatchPlanner accepts memory_estimator callback (spec → bytes); overrides cardinality rules if Vmap memory exceeds device limit.
Heterogeneous axes declared to planner; Scan strategy rejected if axis is heterogeneous (static shape requirement).
gaps: No existing visualization or display layer for BatchPlan, AxisDecision, or AxisStrategy.
No metrics or statistics modules for tiling decisions (e.g., strategy distribution, rule trigger counts).
No CLI or interactive tools for exploring plans (e.g., plan detail, what-if scenario analysis).
Bucket strategy outputs (padded shapes, compiled executable cache) not exposed as metrics.
Dedup statistics (unique count k, padding overhead k_bucket - k, index array distributions) not logged or visualized.
No integration with training/engine layers to surface decision rationale or performance metrics during training.
Test suite covers correctness (phase logic, rule priority, edge cases); no benchmarks or performance profiles for different strategy choices.
suggestions: Design EDA module (xtrax.eda) with submodules: stats (metrics extraction from plan/decision objects), viz (plot helpers), export (dataframe/JSON serialization).
Prototype BatchPlan → dataframe converter: one row per AxisDecision with columns (axis_name, cardinality, batch_size, strategy_type, reasoning, estimated_memory).
Add plan.explain() method or eda.explain_plan(plan) function that renders decision tree with rationale and branching logic (rules 1-5).
Dedup statistics: extract k, k_bucket, unique_indices.shape, padding_waste = k_bucket - k; vizualize as histogram or summary table.
Bucket visualization: show boundaries as horizontal bars with actual input lengths overlaid (what would land in each bucket?).
Consider optional dependency group: eda = [matplotlib, seaborn, pandas] for viz; import with __getattr__ lazy pattern (like training subpackage).
Pre-register hypothesis for EDA API: can we represent all decision outputs (AxisDecision, rationale, strategy payload) as queryable dataframe-like objects without breaking immutability?
notes: All findings anchored to path:line with tool-verified lexical hits. No visualization or EDA code currently exists (confirmed via grep for 'plot|visual|metric'). BatchPlanner.plan() is the core output generating AxisDecision tuples; this is the natural entry point for EDA API. Bucket and DedupGather carry host-side metadata suitable for statistical exploration.
